sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: React is the dominant frontend library in any fullstack Java project using a modern stack. Interviewers test it at every level. For freshers, the core concepts are: Virtual DOM and reconciliation, JSX, functional components, hooks (useState + useEffect), props, and the event model. Understanding these deeply separates candidates who 'know some React' from those who genuinely understand it.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
- **React = a UI description language**: you describe *what* the UI looks like given some state; React figures out *how* to update the DOM efficiently.
- **Virtual DOM**: React maintains a lightweight JS copy of the DOM. On state change, it computes a diff (reconciliation) and only updates what changed.
- **Components = functions**: a React component is just a function that takes props and returns JSX. State is external to the render (via useState).
- **One-way data flow**: data flows down via props; events bubble up via callback props. No two-way binding like Angular.
- **Hooks**: `useState` gives components memory between renders; `useEffect` runs side effects after render; hooks replace class lifecycle methods entirely.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- **react-intro-virtual-dom**: explain Virtual DOM, reconciliation, and why it is faster than direct DOM manipulation.
- **jsx-and-components**: JSX syntax rules, what Babel does, functional vs class components (know class exists, focus on functional).
- **state-with-usestate**: `const [state, setState] = useState(initial)`, why you must not mutate state directly, what triggers a re-render.
- **useeffect-lifecycle**: dependency array controls when the effect runs: `[]` = mount once, no array = every render, `[dep]` = when dep changes; cleanup function.
- **props**: read-only, one-way, can include functions (callbacks), children prop.
- **lists-and-keys**: always add a stable `key` prop when rendering arrays — never use array index unless list is static.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- *"What is the Virtual DOM and how does reconciliation work?"* — React creates a virtual tree, diffs it against the previous on state change, and applies only the minimum DOM updates.
- *"What is the difference between state and props?"* — state is local and mutable (managed by useState); props are external and read-only.
- *"What does the dependency array in useEffect do?"* — it controls when the effect re-runs; empty array = run once on mount; dependencies = run when they change.
- *"Why must you not mutate state directly?"* — React uses object reference equality to detect changes; mutating in place produces the same reference so React doesn't detect the change and re-render.
- *"Why do list items need a `key` prop?"* — keys help React's reconciliation algorithm identify which items changed/added/removed, avoiding full list re-renders.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"React is a declarative UI library. Instead of manually manipulating the DOM, you describe what the UI should look like for a given state, and React handles all the DOM updates efficiently through its Virtual DOM and reconciliation algorithm. Components are pure functions — given the same props and state they always produce the same output. State is managed with useState hooks, side effects like API calls run in useEffect, and data flows one-way from parent to child via props, with child-to-parent communication happening through callback functions passed as props."*
